content: # 2017–18 Bundesliga. | **Champions League** | Bayern Munich Schalke 04 1899 Hoffenheim Borussia Dortmund | |. The **2017–18 Bundesliga** was the 55th season of the Bundesliga, Germany's premier football competition. Bayern Munich were the defending champions and won their 27th Bundesliga title on 7 April with five games to spare, winning a sixth consecutive title for the first time in their history. 1. FC Köln and Hamburger SV were relegated at the end of the season, with the latter therefore losing their status as the only ever-presents in Bundesliga history. On 28 October, a 2–0 win over RB Leipzig put Bayern on top of the table for the first time in the season. On 5 May, Schalke secured second place and a return to the Champions League for the first time in four years, with a 2–1 win at Augsburg.

title: 2017–18 Bundesliga - Grokipedia
content: The 2017–18 Bundesliga was the 55th season of Germany's top-tier professional football league, featuring 18 clubs in a double round-robin format over 34 matchdays from 18 August 2017 to 12 May 2018.](#ref-1)](#ref-2) The season marked the introduction of video assistant referee (VAR) technology across all matches, aimed at improving decision-making accuracy.](#ref-3) Bayern Munich clinched their 28th Bundesliga title and sixth consecutive championship, amassing 84 points from 27 wins, 3 draws, and 4 losses, while scoring a league-high 92 goals and conceding only 28.](#ref-4)](#ref-2) Under interim manager Jupp Heynckes, appointed after Carlo Ancelotti's dismissal in September 2017, Bayern recovered from an early-season stutter to pull clear of challengers, ultimately finishing 21 points ahead of runners-up **FC Schalke 04** (63 points).](#ref-5)](#ref-6) **TSG 1899 Hoffenheim** and **Borussia Dortmund** occupied third and fourth places respectively, both on 55 points, securing Champions League qualification alongside the top two.](#ref-6) **Bayer 04 Leverkusen** rounded out the European spots in fifth with 53 points, qualifying for the Europa League.](#ref-6) The season produced 855 goals at an average of 2.79 per match, with Bayern's Robert Lewandowski claiming the top scorer award (Torjägerkanone) for the third time, netting 29 goals in 29 appearances.](#ref-4)](#ref-7) At the lower end, historic club **Hamburger SV** suffered direct relegation in 18th place with 31 points, ending their 55-year unbroken stay in the top flight amid fan protests and three managerial changes during the campaign.](#ref-8)](#ref-9) **1.
